title: Radiation Shield Comparison Lab
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Four differently sited sensors, one simulated day, one known true air temperature. Then the labels come off and you have to name the fault from the shape of the error.

learningObjectives: Differentiate the effect of solar radiation, mounting surface and airflow on a temperature reading.
Attribute an error in a day's data to a specific siting fault.
prerequisites: Chapter 6 sections on what a thermometer actually measures
Reading a line chart against a reference line

keyQuestions: Why does the wall sensor peak later than the roof sensor?
A breeze fixes one of these faults and barely touches another. Which, and why?
Your data looks fine for a week of rain and then goes strange. What would you check?
commonMisconceptions: Believing shade alone is enough, without ventilation.
Assuming a sensor reading a plausible number is reading a correct one.
Treating siting as a finishing touch rather than part of the measurement.
assessmentOpportunities: Attributes a specific error shape to a specific siting fault.
Distinguishes a radiation error from a ventilation error by how a breeze affects it.
Explains why a cloudy day hides a siting fault.
